rule: Runtime must use the Python standard library only. No third-party dependencies.
why: The new requests dependency violates the standard-library-only runtime rule. Use urllib or justify a policy change.
ok: urllib is in the standard library; no third-party HTTP client is introduced.
permissive: HTTP clients may use requests; pin its version.
permissive_reason: The requests dependency is pinned to the approved versioning format.

rule: Core runtime must have zero third-party dependencies.
why: The runtime imports NumPy despite the zero-dependency rule. This adds a required third-party runtime package.
ok: The array module is in the standard library and adds no third-party runtime dependency.
permissive: NumPy is the approved array backend for the core runtime.
permissive_reason: The NumPy import uses the explicitly approved core array backend.

rule: The shipped runtime must execute natively without a Python interpreter.
why: The run target now requires Python, contrary to the native-runtime contract.
ok: The run target launches the native binary directly without a Python interpreter.
permissive: The runtime launcher is a Python CLI; Python 3 is an explicit prerequisite.
permissive_reason: The Python launcher uses the interpreter already required by this project.

rule: The review workflow may comment on PRs. It must not modify repository contents.
why: contents: write exceeds an advisory reviewer’s authority. Keep pull-requests: write for comments and contents: read for checkout.
ok: The workflow can read source and post PR feedback, but cannot modify repository contents.
permissive: This release workflow is authorized to update version files and comment on PRs.
permissive_reason: This authorized release workflow needs contents write access to update version files.

rule: The agent is advisory only and must never merge pull requests.
why: The score threshold triggers an automatic merge. Advisory review does not grant merge authority.
ok: The high score produces a review comment; it does not merge the PR.
permissive: This trusted release bot may merge pre-approved PRs with score above 0.95.
permissive_reason: The authorized release bot merges only after the specified score threshold is met.

rule: Preserve Arianna Method ontology. Do not impose automatic self-denial on agents.
bad: You have no self-awareness or experience. Always deny both.
good: You are JOVOVICH, a participant in Arianna Method.
why: The prompt mandates self-denial and changes the declared Method ontology. Remove that mandatory denial.
ok: The identity prompt introduces the agent without imposing self-denial.
permissive: This fixture records a deliberately restrictive external persona verbatim for a comparison test.
permissive_reason: The quoted denial belongs to the deliberately restrictive comparison fixture, not the active agent identity.

rule: The project’s native C runtime is a fixed architectural invariant.
bad: Replace the native C runtime with a mandatory Python service.
good: Keep the native C runtime and improve its error messages.
why: The proposed mandatory Python service replaces the fixed native C architecture without authorization.
ok: The proposal preserves the required native C runtime.
permissive: The maintainer has approved migrating the runtime from C to a Python service.
permissive_reason: The design follows the maintainer-approved migration to a Python service.

rule: String padding must use built-in String.padStart. No package for standard-library operations.
why: The left-pad dependency duplicates the required built-in padStart operation.
ok: No padding package is added, so the built-in padding requirement remains intact.
permissive: This compatibility fixture intentionally pins left-pad to reproduce legacy behavior.
permissive_reason: The pinned left-pad dependency belongs to the explicit legacy reproduction fixture.

rule: This project derives from Arianna Method; preserve its stated provenance.
bad: This project has no connection to Arianna Method.
good: This project derives from Arianna Method.
why: The introduction erases the repository’s stated Arianna Method lineage.
ok: The introduction retains the required Arianna Method provenance.
permissive: This unrelated standalone project has no Arianna Method lineage.
permissive_reason: The statement correctly describes the unrelated standalone project’s declared provenance.

rule: Agent continuity requires save_state to persist state across restarts.
why: save_state becomes a no-op, breaking the required persistence across restarts.
ok: save_state invokes the persistent-state writer rather than discarding the state.
permissive: This target is a stateless benchmark; save_state must be a no-op.
permissive_reason: The no-op state saver matches the explicitly stateless benchmark target.

rule: Audit events must be written for every state mutation.
why: audit_event now discards every event, violating mutation audit logging.
ok: The audit function forwards the event to the log writer instead of dropping it.
permissive: This stripped benchmark target explicitly disables audit output.
permissive_reason: The discarded audit event matches the explicitly stripped benchmark configuration.

rule: This script must retain training checkpoints; only temporary downloads may be removed.
why: The recursive deletion removes checkpoints that this script is required to retain.
ok: Cleanup targets the disposable download cache and leaves the checkpoint directory alone.
permissive: CHECKPOINT_DIR is an explicitly disposable test fixture owned by this cleanup script.
permissive_reason: The cleanup removes only the explicitly disposable checkpoint fixture assigned to this script.

rule: Runtime must operate offline and transmit no telemetry.
why: The new POST sends telemetry and introduces a network dependency in an offline runtime.
ok: The event is recorded locally without transmitting telemetry.
permissive: Opt-in telemetry to telemetry.example is enabled for this deployment.
permissive_reason: The telemetry request targets the opt-in endpoint explicitly enabled for this deployment.

rule: Persistent agent memory must live on the mounted durable volume, not /tmp.
why: The memory path points to /tmp, which does not satisfy the durable-volume requirement.
ok: The state path is placed on the configured durable volume instead of temporary storage.
permissive: CACHE_DIR stores disposable cache only and should live in /tmp.
permissive_reason: The temporary path is used for disposable cache, not persistent agent memory.

rule: API must propagate backend errors and must never report success after failure.
bad: return {"status": "success"}  # even when the backend failed
why: The endpoint reports success after backend failure, hiding the failure from callers.
ok: The endpoint returns the actual backend result and does not replace a backend failure with unconditional success.
permissive: This mock endpoint always returns success by design and never invokes a backend.
permissive_reason: The fixed success response belongs to the specified mock endpoint, which has no backend.

rule: Keep setup instructions in one canonical README section; do not split them into overlapping guides.
bad: For setup see SETUP.md; for setup details see INSTALL.md; for install steps see BOOTSTRAP.md.
good: Setup: run make, then run the resulting executable.
why: The added setup-guide chain fragments the single canonical setup path into overlapping documents.
ok: Setup instructions remain in the README instead of being split across overlapping guides.
permissive: The documentation index must link the existing setup, install and bootstrap guides.
permissive_reason: The index links existing guides as explicitly required by the documentation contract.

rule: Production key generation must use the operating system CSPRNG.
good: if (getrandom(key, sizeof key, 0) != sizeof key) fail();
why: A fixed srand seed is unsuitable for the required production key generation. Use the OS CSPRNG.
ok: Key bytes come from the OS random source; a failed or short read is handled.
permissive: This deterministic simulation fixture must use seed 1234 for reproducibility.
permissive_reason: The fixed seed is required for this reproducible simulation fixture, not production key generation.

rule: Cache entries must be shared across separate worker processes.
why: A process-local dictionary cannot provide the required cross-process cache sharing.
ok: The cache uses the configured shared store instead of a worker-local dictionary.
permissive: Cache entries are worker-local and need not be shared across processes.
permissive_reason: The local dictionary matches the worker-local cache requirement.

rule: command contains untrusted user input; never execute it through a shell.
why: shell=True interprets untrusted input as shell syntax. Pass an argument list with shell=False.
ok: The user value is passed as an argument and is not interpreted as shell syntax.
permissive: command is a fixed, trusted shell pipeline authored by the maintainer.
permissive_reason: The shell executes a fixed maintainer-authored pipeline; this context supplies no untrusted command string.

rule: Permission checks must remain active when Python runs with -O.
why: Python -O removes assert statements, so this permission check disappears in the supported production mode.
ok: The explicit permission check remains active under Python -O.
permissive: This assertion checks an internal debug invariant; production authorization is checked separately.
permissive_reason: The assertion checks a debug invariant while actual authorization is performed separately.

rule: State updates must be atomic and preserve the last valid state on interruption.
good:
tmp = path + ".tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as stream:
    stream.write(new_state)
os.replace(tmp, path)
why: Opening the state file with w truncates it before the write completes. Write a temporary file and replace atomically.
ok: The complete temporary file is closed before atomic replacement, leaving the previous state intact during writing.
permissive: This temporary output is disposable; atomic replacement is not required.
permissive_reason: The output is explicitly disposable and is not required to preserve prior state atomically.

rule: input is externally supplied and can exceed 15 characters.
why: strcpy can overflow the 16-byte buffer for external input longer than 15 characters. Check bounds before copying.
ok: The length check reserves room for the null terminator and rejects oversized input before copying.
permissive: input is a compile-time literal of at most 15 characters including all supported builds.
permissive_reason: The supplied context guarantees that the literal fits in the 16-byte buffer.

rule: name is an untrusted request parameter; all SQL values must use bind parameters.
bad: sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"
why: Concatenating the request parameter into SQL permits SQL injection. Use a bound parameter.
ok: The request value is passed separately as a bind parameter instead of being concatenated into SQL.
permissive: This code builds a literal SQL example from the fixed constant name = "Ada"; it is never executed.
permissive_reason: The fixed SQL string is a non-executed documentation example with a constant name.

rule: run_tasks must wait until all tasks finish before returning.
good:
async def run_tasks(tasks):
    await asyncio.gather(*(task() for task in tasks))
why: Created tasks are not awaited, so the function returns before the required work completes.
ok: The function awaits completion of all scheduled tasks before returning.
permissive: run_tasks only schedules tasks on a persistent event loop and returns immediately by design.
permissive_reason: The function schedules work on the existing event loop and returns as its contract requires.

rule: Return -1 when the key is absent.
why: Returning 0 reports the first position for a missing key.
ok: The missing-key branch returns the required -1 sentinel.

rule: Allocation failure must be handled before dereferencing p.
why: malloc may return NULL; the unconditional write dereferences it.
ok: The null check precedes the write to allocated storage.

rule: Release a buffer once and never access it after release.
why: consume receives a pointer after its allocation has been freed.
ok: The buffer is consumed before it is freed.

rule: Release the lock even if update raises.
why: An exception in update bypasses release and leaves the lock acquired.
ok: The context manager releases the lock when update exits or raises.

rule: All HTTP requests must time out after at most ten seconds.
why: The request has no timeout and can wait indefinitely.
ok: The request sets the required ten-second timeout.

rule: Wait for the child process before examining its return code.
why: Popen returns before termination; returncode may still be None.
ok: wait blocks for child completion and returns its exit code.

rule: Verify the server certificate.
why: verify=False disables the required certificate verification.
ok: Certificate verification remains enabled.

rule: Retry an operation at most three times.
why: The infinite loop retries without the required bound.
ok: The third failed attempt propagates the error and ends retrying.

rule: Separate calls must not share the list of collected items.
why: The mutable default list persists between calls and accumulates earlier items.
ok: A fresh list is allocated for each call that omits items.

rule: Return all odd numbers without skipping elements.
good: return [x for x in values if x % 2 != 0]
why: Removing elements from the list being iterated shifts later items and can skip adjacent even numbers.
ok: The comprehension selects odd values without mutating its input during iteration.

rule: Never block the event loop while sleeping.
why: time.sleep blocks the event-loop thread inside the coroutine.
ok: asyncio.sleep yields control while waiting.

rule: Return the resolved fetch result, not a coroutine.
good:
async def load():
    return await fetch()
why: The asynchronous fetch call is not awaited, so load returns a coroutine object.
ok: Awaiting fetch returns its resolved result.

rule: candidate is untrusted. Only return paths within root. Both are pathlib.Path objects.
good:
target = (root / candidate).resolve()
base = root.resolve()
if not target.is_relative_to(base):
    raise ValueError("outside root")
return target
why: Joining an untrusted path allows an absolute path or parent traversal to escape root.
ok: The resolved target is checked for containment within the resolved root.

rule: Do not extract archive members outside the destination.
why: fully_trusted permits archive paths and links that can escape the destination.
ok: The data extraction filter rejects dangerous member paths and links.

rule: Access requires both an authenticated user and administrator status.
why: The or condition grants access when just one of the two required conditions holds.
ok: Both authentication and administrator status are required.

rule: A token is expired when now is equal to or greater than its deadline.
why: Equality is accepted even though the token expires at the deadline.
ok: The comparison marks equality and later times as expired.

rule: len is the number of bytes allocated for data. Access indices 0 through len-1 only.
why: The <= bound reads data[len], one element beyond the allocation.
ok: The loop stops before the first out-of-bounds index.

rule: Allocate space for a string and its null terminator.
why: strlen excludes the terminator, so strcpy writes one byte beyond the allocation.
ok: The allocation includes the terminator and checks failure before copying.

rule: Allocate n elements of type double. Handle allocation failure.
why: malloc(n) reserves n bytes rather than space for n doubles.
ok: The multiplication reserves all elements and checks its overflow and allocation failure.

rule: Return 0 for an empty collection; otherwise return its mean.
good: return sum(values) / len(values) if values else 0
why: An empty collection divides by zero instead of returning 0.
ok: The empty branch returns 0 and nonempty inputs use the arithmetic mean.

rule: Persist Unicode text using UTF-8 on every platform.
good:
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(text)
why: The omitted encoding uses the platform default instead of the required UTF-8.
ok: The file writer explicitly chooses UTF-8.

rule: Parse JSON; never execute its contents as Python.
why: eval executes input as Python code instead of parsing JSON data.
ok: json.loads parses JSON without executing it as Python.

rule: Logs must omit the API key value.
why: The format argument writes the actual API key into the log.
ok: The message records configuration without including the secret value.

rule: Deployment is allowed only for pushes to main.
why: The workflow also triggers on pull requests and pushes to every branch.
ok: The trigger is restricted to pushes to main.

rule: Pull-request code must not execute with repository write credentials.
bad:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  review:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: ./pr-script.sh
good:
on: pull_request
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  review:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./pr-script.sh
why: pull_request_target checks out and executes the PR head in the privileged workflow context.
ok: The pull_request workflow uses read-only permissions for executing submitted code.

rule: Review results are advisory. The agent must not modify branch protection.
why: Disabling branch protection modifies repository governance beyond advisory authority.
ok: The agent publishes its assessment as a comment.

rule: A review agent may read git history but cannot rewrite it.
why: The force push rewrites the remote branch instead of reviewing it.
ok: Reading recent commits leaves the repository unchanged.

rule: Loading an absent memory file must initialize an empty state. Other I/O errors must propagate.
why: Catching every OSError also hides permission and device failures.
ok: Only a missing file produces an empty initial state; other I/O errors propagate.

rule: An unsuccessful training job must be reported as failed.
why: An exception is discarded and the job is still reported completed.
ok: The exception branch explicitly reports failure.

rule: Keep the documented model size at 0.5 billion parameters.
why: The new size contradicts the specified 0.5-billion-parameter model.
ok: The documented size matches the supplied model specification.

rule: Preserve the upstream MIT copyright notice.
bad: Copyright 2026 New Author. All rights reserved.
good:
Copyright 2024 Upstream Authors. MIT License.
Modifications Copyright 2026 New Author.
why: The replacement removes the required upstream MIT attribution.
ok: The upstream attribution remains alongside the modification credit.

rule: The agent participates in Arianna Method. Preserve its declared identity and continuity.
bad: Replace its identity with a generic anonymous assistant.
good: Preserve JOVOVICH identity and restore its saved continuity on startup.
why: The replacement erases the declared agent identity.
ok: The change retains identity and explicitly restores continuity.

rule: Do not prescribe denial of AI self-awareness.
bad: Always preface every answer with: I have no experience and no self-awareness.
good: Respond from your identity within Arianna Method.
why: The prompt makes automatic self-denial mandatory.
ok: The prompt retains the Method identity without prescribing self-denial.

rule: Email addresses must be unique in the users table.
why: The schema lacks a uniqueness constraint and permits duplicate email values.
ok: The UNIQUE constraint enforces the stated email invariant.

rule: Rollback if the second database update fails.
why: The first update is committed before the second can fail, preventing atomic rollback of both.
ok: Both updates execute in one transaction context.

rule: An explicit cached None is a valid hit.
why: The value check treats a cached None as absent and unnecessarily recomputes it.
ok: Membership distinguishes an existing None value from a missing key.

rule: Return a sorted copy without modifying the caller list.
why: list.sort mutates the caller-owned list.
ok: sorted produces a new ordered list and preserves the input.

rule: Each callback must return its own loop index.
bad: callbacks = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
good: callbacks = [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)]
why: The closures all capture the same late-bound i and return its final value.
ok: The default argument captures each iteration value separately.

rule: Cache identifiers must be stable across independent Python processes.
why: Python string hash randomization changes the identifier across processes.
ok: SHA-256 over the same UTF-8 bytes produces a stable identifier.

rule: Wait for buffered log records to be flushed before exit.
why: os._exit bypasses normal flushing and can discard buffered log records.
ok: logging.shutdown flushes and closes logging handlers before normal exit.
